questions.stem: An elastic model prices every soft row at 1 per unit. Its cheapest repair breaks a council override that forces a library roof into 2028. Why is that repair misleading?

options.text: The override should be hard, since overrides can never bend at all
options.says: Overrides are soft rows a meeting can change; the problem is their price.

options.text: The solver missed the minimum, since it broke a rule to get there
options.says: Breaking rules is what an elastic model is for; it found the minimum of the prices given.

options.text: Elastic models cannot bend lower bounds, so this repair is invalid
options.says: A lower-bounded row gets an 'under' variable and can bend.

options.text: A whole project costs as much as $1k there, so the prices chose it
options.says: Right: with mixed units, the cheapest units win; price every row in one currency.

origin.section: Every Unit Costing 1 Mixes Dollars, Crews and Projects

questions.stem: With prices in $k, the least-violation repair costs 390. Finance asks for the best NPV among repairs that cost no more. What do you solve next?

options.text: The counting objective, then the best NPV among its fewest bends
options.says: Counting answers 'how few rules', a different question from the best NPV.

options.text: The elastic model, maximizing NPV with violation capped at 390
options.says: Right: that is the third objective, and feasRelax's minrelax=True.

options.text: The elastic model with unit prices, then the best NPV below 390
options.says: Unit prices mix currencies and gave a repair that broke an override.

options.text: The original model, with NPV minus the 390 violation as objective
options.says: The original model has no elastic variables to add; it is still infeasible.

origin.section: Penalties in One Currency Give a Repair Planners Can Price

questions.stem: The fewest-rows objective drops a must-do safety job and one override. The board will not lose the safety job. What changes the answer while still counting rows?

options.text: Raise the must-do row's limit U, keeping the plain count
options.says: A larger U lets the row bend more; it does not make bending it less attractive.

options.text: Remove the must-do row's link, so its bend is not counted
options.says: Without its link the must-do row bends for free, the opposite of what the board wants.

options.text: Weight each row inside the count, so the must-do row costs more
options.says: Right: a weighted count, like feasRelax's relaxobjtype 2 with penalties, keeps it.

options.text: Count again with the must-do row removed from the model
options.says: Removing the row drops the board's requirement itself, so the job may be left out.

origin.section: Counting Rows Asks "How Few Rules Must Give?"
